PROBLEM_We_Had: Three departments (Engineering, TRD, S&T) plan independently on separate systems — nobody sees the others requests, so overlapping blocks and duplicated work are discovered only after trains are disrupted.
SOLUTION_How_We_Solved: One unified portal brings all three departments block requests onto a single platform, enabling cross-department visibility, AI conflict detection and joint optimization for the first time.

PROBLEM_We_Had: Every block request is typed manually from paper defect registers — slow, error-prone, and overdue tasks slip through unnoticed until they cause failures.
SOLUTION_How_We_Solved: Reads defects and overdue tasks directly from TMS/SMMS/TDMS and auto-generates block requests, eliminating ~80% of paperwork and ensuring nothing overdue is ever missed.

PROBLEM_We_Had: No one knows live which section is blocked or free — planners double-book sections and control rooms argue over outdated lists.
SOLUTION_How_We_Solved: A live block status monitor synced from BDMS/COA data shows blocked/free sections in real time on map and table, ending double-booking.

PROBLEM_We_Had: Blocks are booked with guess-based durations — crews over-estimate to be safe, so sections stay blocked long after work ends and trains wait for nothing.
SOLUTION_How_We_Solved: An AI duration estimator predicts the exact work time from historical records, shrinking over-blocking and returning idle track time to train operations.

PROBLEM_We_Had: A single long block shuts an entire corridor for hours even though the actual work touches only small stretches — massive avoidable disruption.
SOLUTION_How_We_Solved: Splits long blocks into smaller per-segment windows so trains can run on unaffected stretches while maintenance proceeds section by section.

PROBLEM_We_Had: Maintenance competes with dense daytime passenger traffic — every block causes delays, cancellations and passenger complaints.
SOLUTION_How_We_Solved: Analyzes the time table to propose low-traffic night windows, shifting work to hours when passenger impact is minimal.

PROBLEM_We_Had: Gangs are assigned informally by phone — the same crew gets double-booked, distant gangs travel for hours, and block windows expire unused.
SOLUTION_How_We_Solved: Auto-plans crew deployment per block with base-station awareness and shift management, so the right gang is at the right section at the right time.

PROBLEM_We_Had: Blocks get sanctioned without checking if sleepers, rails or machines actually exist — crews arrive, find nothing, and the whole window is wasted ("empty block").
SOLUTION_How_We_Solved: Links block approval to material/tool inventory so a block cannot be sanctioned until everything needed is confirmed available.

PROBLEM_We_Had: When a block clashes with trains, there is no rule for who wins — premium trains like Rajdhani wait arbitrarily, hurting punctuality and reputation.
SOLUTION_How_We_Solved: A priority classifier (Rajdhani > Mail/Express > Passenger > Freight) gives every train a clear tier so block decisions automatically protect premium services.

PROBLEM_We_Had: High-priority trains get stuck behind maintenance blocks because rescheduling is manual and slow.
SOLUTION_How_We_Solved: Fast-track clearance automatically shortens or reschedules blocks around approaching priority trains — with a hard minimum-work-window guard (feature 70) so safety is never compromised.

PROBLEM_We_Had: Officers approve blocks without knowing how many passengers will suffer — impact decisions are pure guesswork.
SOLUTION_How_We_Solved: A passenger impact calculator estimates delayed passengers per block from train schedules and class, producing an objective 0-100 impact score for every decision.

PROBLEM_We_Had: Freight trains squeeze between passenger blocks unpredictably, disrupting both and annoying freight customers.
SOLUTION_How_We_Solved: Dedicated freight slots (mainly night) are carved from the goods forecast so freight moves in predictable windows with minimal passenger disturbance.

PROBLEM_We_Had: Blocks occasionally slip into morning/evening rush hours, causing maximum passenger chaos for minimal maintenance gain.
SOLUTION_How_We_Solved: An auto-guard rejects any block inside configurable peak windows, protecting rush-hour punctuality by design.

PROBLEM_We_Had: Two departments often book the same section at the same time — discovered at the last minute, forcing frantic manual renegotiation while trains wait.
SOLUTION_How_We_Solved: AI conflict detection instantly flags overlapping requests the moment they are created, long before they reach the field.

PROBLEM_We_Had: Resolving a block conflict takes hours of meetings between departments — windows expire while engineers negotiate.
SOLUTION_How_We_Solved: An auto-resolution engine proposes ready alternatives ("ENG at 2pm, TRD at 4pm" or a combined window), cutting negotiation to a single click.
